Read and write DELTA datasets

Source: R/delta.R
readDELTA.Rd

DELTA (DEscription Language for TAxonomy, Dallwitz 1980) is the oldest and still widely used text format for descriptive data, and a TDWG standard. A dataset is classically three files: specs (how many characters there are and of which type), chars (the character list with the states) and items (the taxa, each with its attributes). readDELTA() reads them into a character matrix (see readSDD() for the convention), writeDELTA() writes a matrix as the three files.

Usage

readDELTA(
  specs,
  chars = NULL,
  items = NULL,
  taxon = "Taxon",
  sep = "/",
  inapplicable = NA,
  comments = FALSE
)

writeDELTA(
  x,
  dir,
  characters = NULL,
  taxon = "Taxon",
  sep = "/",
  inapplicable = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  files = c(specs = "specs", chars = "chars", items = "items")
)

Arguments

specs

Path of the specs file, or of a folder holding files named specs, chars and items (any extension, any case).

chars, items

Paths of the chars and items files. May be left out when specs is a folder, or a single file holding everything.

taxon

Name of the taxon column of the matrix.

sep

Separator between the states of a variable taxon in one cell.

inapplicable

For readers, the cell value to give "not applicable" (default NA, the same as unknown). For writers, the cell value that means "not applicable" (default NULL: none).

comments

If TRUE, keep the comments in the names of characters, states and taxa ("pronotum <colour>").

x

A character matrix (data frame), or the list returned by readDELTA(), readSDD(), readLucid() or readXper().

dir

Folder to write the three files into; created if needed.

characters

Optional data frame describing the characters (Character, Type, States, Unit, InapplicableIf); see writeSDD().

title

Title put in the *SHOW line of each file.

files

Names of the three files.

Value

readDELTA() returns a tdwgData list like readSDD(), with matrix, characters (Character, Type, States, Unit, InapplicableIf, Number), taxa (Taxon, Comment) and meta. writeDELTA() returns the paths of the three files, invisibly.

What is read

The directives *CHARACTER LIST, *ITEM DESCRIPTIONS, *CHARACTER TYPES, *NUMBERS OF STATES, *NUMBER OF CHARACTERS, *IMPLICIT VALUES and *DEPENDENT CHARACTERS, wherever in the given files they are (so a dataset kept in one file, or split differently, reads too); other directives are skipped. Character types are unordered multistate (UM, read as "categorical"), ordered multistate (OM, "ordered"), integer (IN, "integer"), real (RN, "real") and text (TE, "text").

Attributes follow the DELTA standard: 12,1/2 (state 1 or 2) and 12,1&2 (1 and 2) both give "state 1/state 2", so the difference between "or" and "and" is not kept; 13,2-3 is a range, which for an ordered character includes the states in between; 14,U is unknown (NA), 15,- not applicable (inapplicable), 16,V variable (all states). Numeric values are kept as written, e.g. "7-8.5" or "(1-)2-3(-4)", which is the numeric notation of the matrix convention. For a text character the cell is the text of the comment (7<possibly two species>). Implicit values are filled in. A dependent character that is not coded is "not applicable" when its controlling character only takes the controlling states; the rule itself is kept in the InapplicableIf column of characters. Variant items (#+) take the attributes they leave out from their main item, as the standard says.

Comments (text in angle brackets) are dropped from the names of characters, states and taxa unless comments = TRUE, and from the attributes of non-text characters; the comment of a taxon name (usually the authority) is kept in taxa$Comment. A name that consists of nothing but a comment (#4. <longevity of plants>/) is that comment. Typesetting marks (the RTF control words DELTA programs use, such as \i{}, \b0{} or \par{}) are removed, and those that stand for a character (\endash{}, \ldblquote{}) become that character. Files that are not valid UTF-8 are read as Windows-1252. The obsolete line sequence numbers are not supported.

The reader was checked against the datasets distributed with Open DELTA (among them the "Grass Genera" sample, a flora of 506 taxa and a virus database of 969 taxa) by comparing every coded attribute with a second, independent parse of the files.

What is written

specs gets the numbers of characters, states and items, the character types, the numbers of states and the dependent characters; chars the character list; items one item per taxon. Every coded cell is written out (no implicit values are used), NA cells are left out, which DELTA reads as unknown, and cells equal to inapplicable are written as -. The states of a variable taxon are joined with / ("or"). A numeric cell that is not a DELTA number or range, and all cells of text characters, are written as comments. Encoding is UTF-8, and lines are wrapped at 78 columns wherever they have a blank to break at.

A few things cannot be written as they are, because DELTA would read them as syntax: angle brackets in a name make a comment (which readDELTA() drops unless comments = TRUE); a star or, in a name, a numero after a blank is put in parentheses ((*), (#)); the blank after a slash in a name is dropped. No file written by dimoose has been read into a DELTA program (Confor, Intkey, Open DELTA).

References

Dallwitz, M. J. & Paine, T. A. (1992 onwards). Definition of the DELTA format. https://www.delta-intkey.com/www/standard.htm

See also

readSDD(), readLucid().

Examples

dir <- system.file("extdata", "tdwg", "beetles-delta", package = "dimoose")
d <- readDELTA(dir)
d
#> Character data "Three beetles" (DELTA) 
#>   3 taxa x 7 characters (3 categorical, 1 ordered, 1 integer, 1 real, 1 text) 
#>   $matrix, $characters, $taxa, $meta
d$matrix
#>                 Taxon antennal club     pronotum           eyes
#> 1 Aphodius exemplaris       present black/yellow of normal size
#> 2      Carabus fictus        absent    red/black     very large
#> 3 Lucanus imaginarius       present        black of normal size
#>                                                                                   frons
#> 1 with setae on anterior middle and above eyes/with setae above eyes only/without setae
#> 2                                                                         without setae
#> 3                                                                                  <NA>
#>   number of lamellae in antennal club     length             comments
#> 1                                   3  (4-)5-6.5       common in dung
#> 2                                <NA>      22-28                 <NA>
#> 3                                 4-6 30-45(-60) possibly two species
d$characters[, c("Character", "Type", "States", "Unit")]
#>                             Character        Type
#> 1                       antennal club categorical
#> 2                            pronotum categorical
#> 3                                eyes categorical
#> 4                               frons     ordered
#> 5 number of lamellae in antennal club     integer
#> 6                              length        real
#> 7                            comments        text
#>                                                                                  States
#> 1                                                                        present/absent
#> 2                                                                      red/black/yellow
#> 3                                                             of normal size/very large
#> 4 with setae on anterior middle and above eyes/with setae above eyes only/without setae
#> 5                                                                                      
#> 6                                                                                      
#> 7                                                                                      
#>   Unit
#> 1     
#> 2     
#> 3     
#> 4     
#> 5     
#> 6   mm
#> 7     

out <- writeDELTA(d, tempfile("delta"))
out
#>                                     specs 
#> "/tmp/RtmpLC0PLY/delta1cae24ef4577/specs" 
#>                                     chars 
#> "/tmp/RtmpLC0PLY/delta1cae24ef4577/chars" 
#>                                     items 
#> "/tmp/RtmpLC0PLY/delta1cae24ef4577/items" 
identical(readDELTA(dirname(out[1]))$matrix, d$matrix)
#> [1] TRUE
